filename: Learning more physically realistic dynamics in machine-learning based weather forecasting with latent-space constraints.pdf
title: Learning more physically realistic dynamics in machine-learning based weather forecasting with latent-space constraints
testbed_rationale: The study develops a training loss formulation for full-state medium-range weather forecasting and data assimilation rather than generating or hosting a reusable benchmark dataset for parameterization testbeds.
pain_points: Standard weighted variable-wise MSE loss neglects cross-variable and spatial error covariances, resulting in smoothed, physically unrealistic long-lead forecasts and kinetic energy loss
The full model-space error covariance matrix exceeds 10^12 dimensions, rendering explicit covariance inversion intractable
Direct estimation of reanalysis error statistics is difficult because the true state of the atmosphere is unobserved
Error covariances are flow-dependent and vary nonlinearly with synoptic conditions
Incorporating multi-source heterogeneous observations into ML training typically requires cumbersome heuristic tuning
extraction_notes: The paper reformulates ML weather forecasting model rollout training through a 4DVar lens, projecting reanalysis error covariance into a Swin Transformer autoencoder latent space where the covariance is approximately diagonal.
